merger_name: HB Land and Satterley – Elimbah Land Joint Venture
merger_description:
Elimbah Land Pty Ltd (**HB Land**) has entered into put and call options for the purchase of four contiguous parcels of land at Elimbah, Queensland, being 181 hectares in area, for the purpose of residential development (the **Property and Option Agreements**).

HB Land and Satterley Elimbah Pty Ltd (**Satterley**) proposes to establish a joint venture entity, Elimbah Land JV Pty Ltd (**ELJV**), to develop the Property and will subscribe for shares in ELJV on a 50/50 basis. HB Land would exercise the options under the Option Agreements in favour of ELJV as nominee, with the intention that ELJV would develop the Property for, principally, residential premises, with the remainder being developed for commercial or industrial purposes.

HB Land is a wholly-owned subsidiary of HB Land Pty Ltd, which is ultimately owned by Ho Bee Land Limited, listed on the Singapore Exchange. In Australia, the HB group is engaged in the development and sale of residential land in Queensland, Victoria and New South Wales.

Satterley is a special purpose investment vehicle, which has been incorporated solely for the purpose of the proposed transaction.

determination_table_content.details:
Elimbah Land Pty Ltd (HB Land) has entered into put and call options
for the purchase of four contiguous parcels of land at Elimbah,
Queensland, being 181 hectares in area, for the purpose of
residential development (the Property and Option Agreements).
HB Land and Satterley Elimbah Pty Ltd (Satterley) proposes to
establish a joint venture entity, Elimbah Land JV Pty Ltd (ELJV), to
develop the Property and will subscribe for shares in ELJV on a
50/50 basis (the Acquisition).
HB Land applied for a notification waiver in respect of the
Acquisition.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

HB Land is a wholly owned subsidiary of HB Land Pty Ltd, which is
ultimately owned by Ho Bee Land Limited, listed on the Singapore
Exchange. In Australia, the HB group is engaged in the development
and sale of residential land in Queensland, Victoria and New South
Wales.
Satterley is a special purpose investment vehicle, which has been
incorporated solely for the purpose of the proposed transaction.
The target, ELJV, is a joint venture entity established between HB
Land and Satterley. HB Land would exercise the options under the
Option Agreements in favour of ELJV as nominee, with the intention
that ELJV would develop the Property for, principally, residential
premises, with the remainder being developed for commercial or
industrial purposes.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. the parties do not currently supply residential land in South
East Queensland
b. there are alternative suppliers of residential land across
South East Queensland and in the local area surrounding
Elimbah
c. the Acquisition does not appear likely to otherwise limit or
prevent competition from rivals.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
